brief: Hungary's sell-side and investor-event stream for banking is small, concentrated and — unusually — largely reconstructable from public records despite the research itself being client-gated. The domestic analyst layer is essentially Concorde, Erste Befektetési, Equilor and OTP's own Global Markets desk, supplemented by ~20 international houses that OTP itself enumerates on its IR analyst page along with downloadable quarterly and annual consensus files; separately, Hungarian issuers file broker target prices to the exchange as formal 'rendkívüli tájékoztatás részvényelemzésről' disclosures on bet.hu/kib_hirek, which is the single highest-leverage lawful route to sell-side signal. The event channel runs through BÉT's own Kibocsátói Fórum, Befektetői Klub and Xmatch programmes (note: 'Kibocsátói Nap' is not the actual name used) plus Portfolio's Hitelezés / Financial IT / Future of Finance conference circuit, both of which publish dated agendas and speaker lists in HU and EN. The weak point is analyst Q&A: OTP earnings-call transcripts were found only on paywalled third-party aggregators, with no issuer-hosted webcast archive located, and the payments sector has no dedicated sell-side channel at all.
